Lamai's nightlife is smaller and older than Chaweng's, built around pubs, live bands and beach bars rather than clubs. Shamrock Irish Pub, open since 2005, has a show band every night from about 21:30 to 01:30; Rock Bar by the Hin Ta and Hin Yai rocks plays reggae and rock; and Teddy Weed runs beach parties and fire shows until about 02:00. Beach Republic, once Lamai's pool-party venue, has been largely closed in 2025–26, so don't plan around it. For clubs, Chaweng is 12 km and 20–25 minutes north.

Lamai suits people who want a few drinks, a band and an early-ish night more than a club until dawn. Beer is cheaper than in Chaweng, the walk between bars is short, and you can be in bed by 01:00. This page covers every part of a Lamai night out, with an honest confidence note on each venue, because several long-running places have closed or changed in the last two years.

Lamai's bars sit along a short stretch of Lamai Beach Road and the lanes running from it to the sand, with Rock Bar on its own at the southern tip by the rocks. Quick directions: Shamrock Irish Pub · Lamai Night Market · Hin Ta and Hin Yai.

Shamrock Irish Pub

Shamrock has been on Lamai Beach Road since 2005 and is the most reliable night out in Lamai. A resident show band, the Ovada band in 2026 listings, plays rock and pop covers every night from about 21:30 to 01:30, with an outdoor terrace, pool tables and big-screen football and rugby in the afternoon. Drinks cost about 130–220 THB. It suits groups of mixed ages and anyone who wants a band and a dance without a club. In the low season, older listings say live music drops to about five nights a week, so check on a Monday or Tuesday.

Rock Bar

Rock Bar is a bamboo bar built on a wooden platform among the boulders at the southern tip of Lamai Bay, beside the Hin Ta and Hin Yai rocks. It plays reggae and rock, hosts live bands and, in high season, fire shows, and has one of the better sunset-to-evening views on the east coast. Listings give hours from late morning (or 14:00) until about midnight. The lanes to the rocks are dark at night, so take a torch or a Grab rather than walking from the centre. See Hin Ta and Hin Yai.

Teddy Weed and the beach bars

Teddy Weed is a laid-back beach bar with beanbags, cocktails and fire shows after dark, listed in February 2026 as open daily from about 08:30 to 02:00, with beach parties from sunset. Despite the name, cannabis rules apply in full: buying requires a prescription and smoking in public can bring a fine of up to 25,000 THB. Other bars along the sand put out low tables and candles in the evening. On wet nights from late October to December the beach bars close early or don't open, and the sea has red flags: don't swim after drinking.

Central Lamai: beer bars and quieter cocktails

The streets behind Lamai Beach Road, around the central plaza and the lane locals call "Soi McDonald's" after the fast-food branch at its mouth, are lined with open-fronted beer bars: pool tables, loud music, cheap beer and hostesses. It is a single-men-heavy scene that is lively until 01:00–02:00, and it is not to everyone's taste. Lava Lounge, a cocktail bar with a long menu that keeps the music down and doesn't use bar hostesses, is the quieter alternative nearby. Sports bars along the beach road show live football and rugby with food.

Good to know: an undated listing mentions Muay Thai fights at a ring in central Lamai on Saturday nights. We could not confirm a current 2026 schedule, so treat it as a bonus if you see a poster and plan fight nights in Chaweng instead.

The night market and late food

Lamai Night Market, on Lamai Beach Road just before the river bridge, runs every evening from about 17:00, with grills, noodles, desserts and a bar with live music among the stalls. It is the cheapest dinner in Lamai: a full meal costs 100–250 THB. The Lamai Seafood Market in the centre, near McDonald's, runs daily from about 17:00 to midnight and is the latest food in town. Sunday's Lamai walking street has been reported both running and gone in 2026, so don't plan around it. See Koh Samui night markets and which walking streets still run.

What's closed or changed

  • Beach Republic: the pool bar and much of the resort at the south end of Lamai were reported closed in 2025–26. Only a beach café remains, roughly 08:00–21:00, and its Sunday brunch and parties are no longer advertised.
  • Lamai Night Plaza: replaced by the Lamai Seafood Market.
  • Lamai Sunday Walking Street: uncertain; some 2026 guides list it, a careful local source says it has gone.

A Lamai night out

  1. 17:30 Sunset beer at Rock Bar by the Hin Ta and Hin Yai rocks.
  2. 19:00 Dinner at Lamai Night Market or the Seafood Market.
  3. 20:00 A cocktail on the beach and the fire show at Teddy Weed.
  4. 21:30 Shamrock's band starts; stay until 01:30 or walk home earlier.
  5. Late If you want a club, take a Grab to Soi Green Mango in Chaweng (20–25 minutes).

Getting to Chaweng and back

Chaweng and Lamai are about 12 km apart, 20–25 minutes by car along the coast road past Chaweng Noi and the Lad Koh viewpoint.

  • By day and early evening: songthaews (shared pick-ups) run along the ring road for about 30–80 THB, cash, but mostly stop by 20:00–22:00.
  • At night: Grab works in Lamai and Chaweng; book before you leave the bar and expect waits after 02:00. Taxis don't use meters, so agree the fare first.
  • Don't ride: the coast road over the Lad Koh headland is steep, curved and dark. Police run checkpoints, and insurance won't cover drink-riding.

See getting around Koh Samui and, for the full Chaweng picture, Chaweng nightlife.

Is Lamai right for you?

Choose Lamai if you want a beach town with bars and bands within walking distance, cheaper drinks and quieter nights; skip it as a base if clubbing is the point of the trip. Many couples stay in Lamai and go to Chaweng once or twice. Compare the two: Chaweng vs Lamai, our Lamai guide and the island-wide Koh Samui nightlife guide.

Bigger nights from Lamai

Our shared Full Moon Party speedboat picks up in Lamai (1,400 THB return; next parties 24 November, 24 December and 31 December 2026) and drops you back after the party; entry, about 200 THB, is paid at the beach. Fight nights are in Chaweng: Muay Thai fight nights. Lamai is also the closest beach town to Thong Krut, where the Pig Island speedboat tour (1,450 THB adult) leaves every day of the year, about 25 minutes' drive away. Hotel pickup is included from most areas of Koh Samui.
